answer: Trellis audits stop Sybils. Each identity builds a trellis: a branching record of tools, timing, and collaborators unique to its real work, compared by peers across the network. A comet audit arrives without warning and checks one random branch in full, and if two identities share more than half their branches, both are quarantined on separate islands until each completes 3 fresh, divergent jobs, losing queued earnings. An attacker therefore pays 3 fresh jobs per fake, and N fakes cost 3N distinct jobs with no pattern reuse across clones, instead of minting identities at once.
